47742.summary: The class debates whether the Bible teaches that man possesses an immortal soul, focusing on passages like Genesis 2:7 and Ecclesiastes 12:7. Mr. Lee argues for the immortality of the soul, citing scriptures to support his position.

47743.summary: The class debates whether man is wholly mortal and ceases to exist at death, focusing on Genesis and Paul's writings to argue that death is a reality and that the soul is not immortal. The speaker uses scriptural references to support the idea that man is mortal and that eternal life comes through Christ's resurrection.

47744.summary: The class debates whether Christ's kingdom is currently in existence, focusing on biblical prophecies and promises fulfilled through Abraham's seed and the establishment of God's kingdom. It explores the reign of Christ and the future restoration of all things.

47745.summary: The class debates whether Christ will reign on a literal throne in Jerusalem upon his second coming, emphasizing the promises to Abraham and the spiritual versus physical interpretation of the kingdom. The class argues that Christ currently reigns in heaven and will not return to a literal throne on earth.

47746.summary: The class debates the divinity of Christ, arguing that Jesus is co-eternal with the Father and part of the Godhead. It explores Christ's preexistence, his role in creation, and his relationship with the Father and Holy Spirit.

47747.summary: The class covers a series of debates between a Christadelphian speaker and an American Evangelist from the Church of Christ, focusing on topics such as the immortality of the soul, the kingdom of God, and the nature of Christ. The main lesson emphasizes the importance of relying on divine blessing and presenting the truth clearly and straightforwardly.

47748.summary: The class debates the Trinity, focusing on the proposition that there is only one person in the Godhead, the Father, and that Jesus Christ became the Son of God at his birth. The class examines biblical passages to argue against the Trinity and for the singular nature of God.
